givesYourCountryPoliticalPowerPp: Gives your country political power (PP). PP is spent appointing advisors, switching laws, and enacting decisions. The value can be positive or negative — a negative subtracts PP. Typical magnitudes: completing a focus +50~150, large decisions +200~400; passive gain ~2 PP/week (BASE_POLITICAL_POWER_INCREASE + modifiers). Cap +2000, floor -500 (defines/POLITICAL_POWER_UPPER_CAP/LOWER_CAP), clamped automatically.
adjustsYourCountrysStabilityAsA: Adjusts your country's stability, as a 0.0~1.0 decimal (not a percentage). 0.05 = +5%. Stability affects factory output, political support, and event probability. Typical magnitudes: small events ±0.01~0.05, major focuses ±0.10, crisis events -0.15~-0.30. The result is clamped to 0.0~1.0. Negatives punish player choices (coups/riots/defeats).
adjustsYourCountrysWarSupportIn: Adjusts your country's war support, in the same 0.0~1.0 decimal as stability. War support determines whether you can conscript, use total-mobilization laws, and unlock aggressive military decisions. Typical magnitudes: small events ±0.01~0.05, being attacked / major events +0.15~0.30, defeat/surrender events -0.20~-0.40. Clamped to 0.0~1.0. Often combined with conscription-law effects to drive a mobilization arc.
scopeChangePicksOneRandomState: Scope change: picks one random state your country owns and actually controls, then runs the inner effect. Conditions inside limit = {} (e.g. free_building_slots > 0) decide which states enter the random pool. Common for 'build a factory / add infrastructure in any qualifying state'. Variants: every_owned_controlled_state (run on all matching states), random_state (random across the whole map). This template: +2 shared slots + 1 mil factory + 1 civ factory.
activatesTheGivenMissionACountdown: Activates the given mission (a countdown task that fires periodically). Missions are defined under common/decisions/ categories, identified by the `days_mission_timeout = N` field (not finishing within N days counts as failure/timeout). An optional `activation = {}` block defines MTTH auto-activation conditions; this effect bypasses that and forces it open. Common for time-limited tasks triggered by a focus chain (e.g. GER_mefo_bills_mission, Maginot Line construction).
firesTheGivenEventForYour: Fires the given event for your country. id format is `namespace.number`, matching an add_namespace in events/xxx.txt. Optional params: days (integer delay), hours, random_hours, random_days (random window). Cross-country firing needs an outer scope change: TAG = { country_event = { ... } }. Note: events with is_triggered_only = yes can only fire via this effect, and aren't scanned by MTTH.
grantsAResearchBonusToThe: Grants a research bonus to the current research. Sub-fields: name (bonus identifier, queryable via has_tech_bonus), bonus (coefficient, 0.5 = +50%), uses (number of uses, 1 = single), category (filter a tech category like infantry_tech) or technology (a single tech ID). Typical magnitudes: small focus 0.5 × 1~2 uses, large focus 1.0 × 2~3 uses. ahead_reduction can lower the ahead-of-time penalty.
activatesAnAdvisorOfTheTarget: Activates an advisor of the target country (the character must already define an advisor role block in common/characters/). Scope change to TAG first, then call activate_advisor with the character_id. Common for 'unlock a hidden advisor after a focus completes'. Distinctions: activate_advisor puts the advisor into the usable slot pool; add_advisor_role (the Level B API) supports a temporary side role; deactivate_advisor removes it.
recruitsACharacterOfTheTarget: Recruits a character of the target country (the character_id must already be defined in common/characters/). Covers every role: country leader, general, field marshal, admiral, scientist, advisor. Difference from activate_advisor: recruit_character is generic recruitment (puts the character into the usable pool) and doesn't auto-assign a post; activate_advisor only targets advisors and auto-fills the advisor slot. Common for 'a focus/event unlocks a famous general/scientist'.
createsAWarGoalEstablishingA: Creates a war goal, establishing a legal casus belli but **not** starting the war immediately. It must be paired with declare_war_on = TAG to actually trigger. Common type values: annex_everything (annex) / puppet_wargoal_focus (puppet) / liberate (free a puppet) / take_state_focus (take states, needs generator params). target is the 3-letter TAG of the target. Large mods pair it with ai_strategy to steer the AI per the script.
addsRecruitedReservesToYourCountrys: Adds recruited reserves to your country's manpower pool. The value is a head count (integer), positive or negative — a negative subtracts manpower. Typical magnitudes: small events +5K~20K, large recruitment focuses +50K~200K, failure costs -10K~-50K. Note: it's the conscription pool, not total population or army size. The pool cap is set by conscription law; excess doesn't stack; exhaustion makes has_manpower < 0 true.
switchesYourCountrysRulingPartyRuling: Switches your country's ruling party. ruling_party valid values: democratic / fascism / communism / neutrality. Optional sub-fields: elections_allowed (whether elections run), last_election (date of the last election), election_frequency (months between elections). It doesn't change the support distribution — to adjust support too, use add_popularity or set_popularities. Common after a coup/civil-war victory; routine switches need a PP-cost event.
addsADiplomaticOpinionModifierToward: Adds a diplomatic opinion modifier toward a country (the modifier must be predefined in common/opinion_modifiers/). target = TAG is the country whose opinion changes; modifier is the opinion_modifier id (common vanilla: large_increase/medium_increase/small_increase + the reverse large_decrease etc.). Common for improving relations on focus completion/events. Distinct from targeted_modifier (a country modifier embedded in an idea/decision) — opinion_modifier is the standalone diplomatic-relations system.
removesAnOpinionModifierPreviouslyAdded: Removes an opinion modifier previously added with add_opinion_modifier. target and modifier must match the values used when adding for the removal to match. Common when declaring war / breaking with an ally (to withdraw a friendly buff), or when switching focus paths (to clear a prerequisite modifier). If the modifier has no decay field in common/opinion_modifiers/, it must be removed explicitly or it stacks permanently.
setsACountryLevelBooleanFlag: Sets a country-level boolean flag. Optional days field for auto-expiry: set_country_flag = { flag = FLAG_NAME days = 30 }. Query with has_country_flag = FLAG_NAME. Common pattern: a decision sets a flag → a modifier applies during that period → days_remove clears it on expiry via clr_country_flag. FLAG_NAME uses snake_case, author-defined, no predefinition needed.
clearsACountryLevelBooleanFlag: Clears a country-level boolean flag previously set with set_country_flag. FLAG_NAME must match the one used when setting. Often used inside a hidden_effect block for state-machine resets (to avoid exposing internal flags in a tooltip). If set_country_flag set a days auto-expiry, an explicit clr_country_flag isn't needed. The state-scope equivalent is clr_state_flag.
assignsANumericVariableVarName: Assigns a numeric variable. VAR_NAME is a snake_case custom variable name (no predefinition needed). value can be a constant / @constant / another variable. Common for passing numbers across entities, caching computations, driving dynamic modifiers (with dynamic_modifier). In a state scope the variable lives on the state, in a country scope on the country. Query with check_variable. set_temp_variable is a function-local variable.
addsToSubtractsFromAVariable: Adds to / subtracts from a variable (a negative value subtracts). The variable must first be initialized with set_variable (otherwise it accumulates from 0, which may not be what you want). Pair with while_loop_effect for loop counting (each pass add_to_temp_variable counter += 1). Same family as multiply_variable / divide_variable / modulo_variable. Variable values persist and don't reset.
wrapperHidesTheInnerEffectFrom: Wrapper: hides the inner effect from the tooltip (doesn't tell the player what it did). Common in immediate blocks to clear flags / reset variables / update a state machine internally. The inverse of effect_tooltip (show a tooltip but don't actually execute). A standard HOI4 idiom — vanilla uses it heavily to hide 'pure mechanical' state operations and avoid tooltip noise.
wrapperShowsTooltipContentButDoesnt: Wrapper: shows tooltip content but doesn't actually run the effect. Common in multi-branch if statements to give the player consistent expectations (every branch shows the same outcome, but only one branch actually executes). Or where a focus preview / decision description needs a tooltip without a double fire. The inverse of hidden_effect (execute but don't show). An indispensable HOI4 idiom.
repeatsTheInnerEffectUntilLimit: Repeats the inner effect until limit is no longer met. Common for 'pick N random states and do X' / batch assignment / counted iteration. A break = name field can explicitly break out early. Note: HOI4 has a built-in infinite-loop guard (default max 1024 iterations), aborting automatically beyond that. Pair check_variable + add_to_temp_variable for the counter. For advanced array loops see reference: 高级代码/数组循环.
randomOwnedStateSaveEventTarget:
random_owned_state = { save_event_target_as = my_state }
# Later available: event_target:my_state = { add_buildings = { ... } }
insideImmediateHiddenEffectMarksA: Inside immediate / hidden_effect, marks a scope as a named target; later effects / options reference it via event_target:NAME. It auto-clears when the event finishes (valid within the same event). Or use save_global_event_target_as to persist across events (clear explicitly with clear_global_event_target). Common idiom: lock 'this_specific_state' while iterating states, or pick 1 of multiple countries and save it as a target. See reference: 高级代码/event_target讲解.
hintsAStrategicTendencyToThe: Hints a strategic tendency to the AI (not forced — just a weight adjustment). Common type values: befriend / antagonize / conquer / contain / declare_war / alliance / influence / area_priority / prepare_for_war, plus 40+ types. value is a weight (commonly 50-200, negative reverses). Common for steering the AI to act per the script. For details see reference: AI战略编写模板扩充版.txt.
addsAContributionToGlobalWorld: Adds a contribution to global world tension (default +1 = +1% tension); the threat field is the value. name is a localisation key shown in the world-tension tooltip (telling the player 'country XX did YY, causing +N% tension'). Common for aggressive-action storylines / a mod's custom tension driver. The reverse is reduce_world_tension.
